凌 has two useful branches: enduring or getting through a difficulty, and surpassing something else. In 凌ぐ (しのぐ), the context selects between these branches. 凌駕 (りょうが) concerns surpassing, not sheltering from bad weather.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: imagine the two 冫 marks as drops beside the right-hand 夌 shape, pictured as a barrier. Think of weathering the drops or getting beyond the barrier. This is an invented memory scene, not a historical derivation or a verified explanation of the sound.

Both readings in the frozen KANJIDIC2 record are selected for practice. Its grade-9/name-use classification does not make these ordinary word readings personal-name readings; names are not taught here.
凌ぐ しのぐ — endure or pull through; surpass
凌駕 りょうが — surpassing; outdoing, also with する
凌ぐ is a ぐ-ending verb: しのぎます, しのいで, しのいだ. Do not confuse it with the separate verb 忍ぶ (しのぶ), which ends in ぶ.
陵 (りょう; みささぎ) has 阝 on the left rather than 凌's two 冫 strokes. Recognizing the rarer spelling 陵駕 (りょうが) does not make these characters freely interchangeable in other words.
Compare 准, "quasi-; associate rank," with 隹 on the right; 冶, "smelt; work metals," with 台; and 次, "next," with 欠. Similar left-hand marks do not imply the same meaning.
Metadata: KANJIDIC2, database 2026-306, 2026-11-02 (EDRDG; CC BY-SA 4.0). Words: JMdict, entries 1554200, 1606270 and 1467450. Usage: Digital Daijisen: 凌ぐ and 凌駕.
凌ぐ しのぐ — endure or pull through; surpass

凌ぐ can mean endure, keep out, or get through something difficult. It can also mean surpass or outdo someone or something in ability, degree or quality. Learn the whole phrase rather than assigning one English equivalent to every occurrence.
風雨を凌ぐ (ふううをしのぐ) — shelter from wind and rain
前作を凌ぐ傑作 (ぜんさくをしのぐけっさく) — a masterpiece surpassing the previous work
These short phrases illustrate the two branches. The difficulty faced or the thing surpassed takes を. 凌ぐ is a transitive godan verb ending in ぐ: しのぎます, しのいで, しのいだ, しのがない.
凌 supplies the enduring or surpassing idea. The native verb is しのぐ: ぐ is written as okurigana, while 凌 represents しの-. The same word, not a different reading, has both meaning branches.
こらえる and 我慢 (がまん), with する, overlap in endurance. Their restraint uses do not all transfer to 凌ぐ. 凌駕 (りょうが), with する, overlaps with the surpassing branch, not with sheltering from the weather.
忍ぶ (しのぶ) is a separate verb that can also mean endure. Its ending is ぶ, not 凌ぐ's ぐ: do not confuse しのいで with しのんで.

Getting through a difficulty does not by itself promise a permanent solution. Conversely, 凌ぐ is not restricted to brief emergencies. In a comparison, it means going above the other thing, not merely matching it. The weather phrase above expresses protection or endurance; the masterpiece phrase expresses comparative quality.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1554200, senses 1–3; comparisons 2827352, 1196970, 1606270 and 1467450. Usage and short example phrases: Digital Daijisen: 凌ぐ, senses 2 and 4.
凌 supplies the enduring or surpassing idea. The native verb is しのぐ: ぐ is written as okurigana, while 凌 represents しの-. The same word, not a different reading, has both meaning branches.
凌駕 りょうが — surpassing; outdoing, also with する
凌駕 names surpassing or outdoing another thing. It is a noun and a する-verb: 凌駕する, 凌駕します, 凌駕した, 凌駕しない. The thing surpassed takes を.
前作を凌駕する売れ行き (ぜんさくをりょうがするうれゆき) — sales surpassing those of the previous work
Here the comparison concerns sales, not a claim that the new work is artistically better. The context determines the dimension being compared.

凌 contributes surpassing, read リョウ here. 駕 (ガ) also has a rising-above-others sense, documented with this compound. The two reinforce the surpassing idea; do not force 駕's separate vehicle meaning into a literal story about this word.

凌ぐ (しのぐ) overlaps in surpassing, but also has endurance and weather-protection uses that 凌駕 does not share. 優れる (すぐれる) describes excellence or superiority; it is an intransitive verb, so its grammar is not 凌駕する's object + を pattern.
上回る (うわまわる), "exceed; surpass," also suits numerical comparisons. These related words are not unrestricted substitutes in every phrase.
凌駕する means going above the comparison target, not simply reaching the same level. Identify what is surpassed and in what respect. It is not a general expression for surviving a hardship.
陵駕 (りょうが) is also recognized, but JMdict marks that spelling as rarely used. This does not make the pronunciation りょうが rare or make 凌 and 陵 freely interchangeable elsewhere.
